newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian arrested for spying for U.S, agencies say.
newsitem.headline: Russian arrested for spying for U.S, agencies say.

text.p: A Russian working at a defence ministry research institute has been arrested on suspicion of spying for the United States, Russian news agencies quoted a source in the FSB security service as saying on Wednesday.

The FSB, which is responsible for counter-intelligence, was not immediately available for comment on the reports by Interfax and Itar-Tass news agencies, which said the man had offered secret information about a new generation of nuclear submarines.
The U.S. embassy in Moscow declined comment.

Tass named the man as Finkel and said he had been employed at a naval research institute in St Petersburg, Russia's second city. It said he had offered the secret information in the hope of winning political asylum in the United States.
Interfax named him as Finkin and said he had been working at a defence ministry institute in St Petersburg.
Neither of the agencies made clear when the man had been arrested.
Some Western officials have expressed alarm at huge sums Moscow is pouring into new attack submarines which are intended to play a much more aggressive role than in the past.

Experts say the Russians have been developing submarines designed to roam the oceans in the hunt for large vessels and other submarines. They say the submarines are quieter than their Western counterparts and have more effective weapons.
